sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Kennewick?
sections.html:
Kennewick sellers can put the house on the market with an agent, sell it directly to another household, or accept a purchase from a buyer who pays cash. The best fit comes down to your timeline, your repair list and how much you owe.

  • Agent sale: Your house is prepared, shown and negotiated. It suits a home in good shape and an owner who can wait for the right buyer.
  • Private sale: You take on pricing, marketing and the contract. The savings come with more work.
  • Cash purchase: The buyer does not need a lender, which removes loan approval from the schedule. Compare any offer on the amount you would receive at closing.

sections.h2: Where is Kennewick, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Kennewick sits in Benton County on the southwest bank of the Columbia River, just southeast of where the Columbia and Yakima rivers meet. It is the most populous of the three Tri-Cities, with Richland upstream on the same side and Pasco across the river. The city covers 29.962 square miles, 28.570 of them land. The 1996 discovery of Kennewick Man, a skeleton roughly 9,300 years old, is one marker of how long people have lived here.

The city was incorporated on February 5, 1904. In the 1890s a company installed pumps and ditches to bring irrigation water to the Kennewick Highlands, and orchards, vineyards and strawberries followed. The Port of Kennewick formed in 1915, the Green Bridge to Pasco opened in 1922, and the Blue Bridge followed in 1954. The Hanford site opened in 1943, and between 1940 and 1950 Kennewick grew from 1,918 residents to 10,085. Interstate 82 reached the area in 1986.

Wikipedia calls Kennewick the retail hub of the Tri-Cities, home to Columbia Center Mall, with other shopping in the historic downtown and the Southridge district. Hanford and the national laboratory still shape the economy, alongside agriculture and health care. Lamb Weston has offices in the city and Tyson Foods processes here, and Trios hospital sits in Southridge.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about housing in Kennewick?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts Kennewick's median home value at $370,700 and shows steady population growth. Housing and income values are 2020 to 2024 estimates.

sections.h2: How do the Kennewick climate and water supply affect a house?
sections.html:
Kennewick has a semi-arid climate that borders on desert, because the Cascades block rain from the west. Precipitation is closer to Phoenix than to Seattle, and the mountains keep the Pacific from moderating temperatures, so extremes run higher. Winter temperature inversions in the basin can bring dense fog that lasts several days, and a 2009 dust storm obscured parts of the city in satellite images.

Flooding is part of the record. The worst Columbia River flood came in 1948, caused one death and about $50 million in damage, and led to the McNary Levee System. The flood threat from the river has fallen since the dams were built. Zintel Canyon Dam near the Southridge Sports and Events Complex protects parts of the city from a 100-year flood, but summer thunderstorms over the Horse Heaven Hills can still send flash floods down the dry creek.

Water works differently here than in many cities. The city provides drinking water and sewer, Benton Public Utility District supplies electricity, and Cascade Natural Gas provides gas. Many owners water lawns with irrigation water from nearby rivers, delivered separately by the Kennewick Irrigation District, or the Columbia Irrigation District on parts of the east side. Ask the district that serves your address for any assessment balance before closing.

sections.h2: What do I pay and file with Benton County when I sell?
sections.html:
The Benton County Treasurer collects property tax for the county, the cities, school districts, fire departments and other taxing districts, based on valuations set by the Assessor. The Kennewick office is at 7122 W Okanogan Pl, Suite E110, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and reachable at 509-735-8505. The treasurer's page currently lists an office closure for Thanksgiving, so plan a late-November closing around it.

  • Property tax: Under RCW 84.56.020, when the total is $50 or more, half is due by April 30 and the second half by October 31. A payment is delinquent after those dates.
  • Excise tax: The seller usually pays Washington's real estate excise tax. At the median value of $370,700, state tax at 1.1 percent comes to about $4,078, since the price stays within the first $525,000 bracket.
  • Forms: The treasurer's forms page lists the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit, a supplemental statement and a refund request.

The Department of Revenue states that excise tax is due to the county treasurer on the sale date, with penalty and interest if unpaid after one month. Your escrow officer will normally prepare the affidavit.

sections.h2: Which projects need a permit in Kennewick?
sections.html:
Some do not, which helps if you are fixing small things before a sale. Kennewick's Building Safety Division lists exceptions to building permits: detached residential accessory structures up to 200 square feet that meet setbacks and stay off easements, retaining walls up to 4 feet high, finish work such as painting, tiling, carpeting and cabinets, prefabricated pools under 24 inches deep, and window awnings that project no more than 54 inches.

New single-family residences of up to two units skip a land use permit, but they still need a building permit. For any question, call Building Safety at 509-585-4276 or Community Planning at 509-585-4280.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and transit shape buyer interest in Kennewick?
sections.html:
Interstate 82 bypasses the city to the south and links to Seattle by way of I-90 and to Portland by way of I-84. U.S. 395 runs north to south, State Route 240 crosses the Blue Bridge to Pasco, and State Route 397 crosses the Cable Bridge. Ben Franklin Transit runs routes through two transit centers, Three Rivers near the Toyota Center and Dayton Transfer Point downtown. The nearest commercial airport is the Tri-Cities Airport in Pasco, whose busiest route goes to Seattle-Tacoma.

Kennewick School District operates 17 elementary schools, five middle schools and three high schools, and serves over 18,000 students. The Tri-Tech Skills Center offers programs such as firefighting, radio broadcasting and auto body technology.

sections.h2: What should I confirm before accepting an offer on my Kennewick house?
sections.html:
• Get the price, the closing date and every cost assigned to you in writing.
  • Request a payoff statement from your lender, then subtract it, the excise tax and any irrigation district balance to see your real proceeds.
  • Ask the buyer to explain how the purchase will be funded and what, if anything, depends on an inspection.
  • Check with Building Safety about any shed, addition or remodel you are unsure was permitted.
  • Ask the Benton County Treasurer for the current tax status on your parcel.

faqs.q: Which county is Kennewick in, and where do I pay property tax?
faqs.a: Benton County. The Benton County Treasurer collects property tax for the county, the city and school districts. The Kennewick office is at 7122 W Okanogan Pl, Suite E110, and the phone number is 509-735-8505.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Benton County house?
faqs.a: One-half is due by April 30 and the remainder by October 31, according to RCW 84.56.020. Payments after those dates are delinquent and carry interest and penalties. Ask the treasurer for a current statement on your parcel.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to put up a shed in Kennewick?
faqs.a: Not always. A detached residential accessory structure up to 200 square feet is exempt from a building permit if it meets setbacks and stays off easements. Larger sheds need a building permit. Call Building Safety at 509-585-4276.

The Kennewick School District serves the city's public schools, with 17 elementary schools, five middle schools and three high schools. It serves over 18,000 students and helps fund the Tri-Tech Skills Center.

faqs.q: Does the Columbia River still flood Kennewick?
faqs.a: The risk from the river has dropped since the dams and the McNary Levee System were built, after the 1948 flood. Flash floods from the Horse Heaven Hills can still occur in Zintel Canyon during summer thunderstorms. Ask the city for the status of your parcel.
